title: The end of Pyrrhus?
html_source:
After Asculum, Pyrrhus continued to barnstorm around the Mediterranean world, which was in a limbo of small-state anarchy with rivalries and lost causes enough for all the ambitious.

His “end” came in 272 BC: Pyrrhus had undertaken to assist one of the leading citizens of Argos in a town feud. His opponent was Antigonus II of Macedon. Pyrrhus was trapped inside the town; when he attempted to slip out, he was caught up in a street fight and was about to kill one of his assailants when the assailant’s mother threw a tile from a roof. Pyrrhus was stunned, thrown from his horse, and killed by one of Antigonus’s henchmen.
